似然回答的问题：如果某个假设成立，手头这批数据出现的可能性有多大。它固定数据、比较假设，方向和后验概率正好相反——后验回答的是：看到数据之后，这个假设本身有多可信。

例子：抛一枚硬币10次，出现9次正面。若硬币均匀（正面概率0.5），似然≈10×0.5¹⁰≈0.0098；若正面概率是0.9，似然≈10×0.9⁹×0.1≈0.387。同一批数据，不同假设给出不同的似然值，0.9那个假设更受数据支持。

但似然高不等于证实。后验 ∝ 似然 × 先验：还要乘上你看到数据前对每个假设的信任程度，再归一化。如果你本来就坚信硬币公平，即使似然差别很大，后验的变化也会打折。有限数据下，似然只是证据，后验才是结合证据与原有信念后的判断。

Variance measures how far numbers typically sit from their average. Two datasets can share a mean and differ wildly in spread: {3,3,3} and {1,3,5} both average 3, but the second is clearly more scattered.

Computing it: take each value's distance from the mean — for {1,3,5}: -2, 0, +2. Plain distances cancel out (they always sum to zero, which is what an average guarantees), so we square them: 4, 0, 4. Squaring fixes the cancellation and also emphasizes large deviations. Then average the squares: (4+0+4)/3 ≈ 2.67. That's the population variance — dividing by 3 because we have all three values.

Change one value to {1,3,11} and the mean moves to 5 while variance jumps to about 18.7: a single outlier dominates.

Variance is in squared units, so taking its square root gives the standard deviation, back in the original units — the typical distance from the mean.

正反馈是把输出的结果送回输入端，让变化沿原方向进一步加强。回路里每转一圈，偏差都被乘上一个大于1的系数，所以哪怕起点很小，也会越滚越大。

麦克风对着音箱是看得见的例子：一点微小的声音被音箱放大播出，又被麦克风拾取、再次放大，几圈之后变成刺耳的啸叫。抢购也一样：价格一涨，'怕更贵'的心理驱动更多人买入，把价格推得更高。

'正'指的是方向——放大而非收敛；'好''坏'是另一回事。正反馈会放大学习带来的自信，也会放大争吵和银行挤兑：一个人取款引发恐慌，恐慌引发更多人取款。评价要看它放大的是什么。

另外，放大不会无限持续：资金、注意力、物理强度总有上限，逼近上限时系统会突然失稳。让局面可控的通常是负反馈——每偏离一点就被往回拉一点。

Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you give up when you pick one. Your free afternoon has three realistic uses: rest, study for Monday's exam, or hike. If you hike, the cost is not 'everything else' — it's the single best foregone option, say studying, which you expect to raise your grade. That benefit is what hiking really costs you, even though no money changes hands; time is the resource, and spending it one way means it can't be spent another.

So the decision question becomes: is the hike worth more to me than the next best use of those hours? Two cautions: only count real alternatives (if you'd never have studied anyway, that's not the cost), and ignore anything already spent earlier — sunk costs don't belong in this afternoon's comparison.

核心问题：检测出阳性后，真患病的概率是多少？答案是约17%，远低于检测准确率。贝叶斯公式解释了为什么。

设10000人体检，患病率1%：
- 患者100人，检测准确率99%，阳性约99人；
- 健康人9900人，误报率5%，阳性约495人。

阳性总人数 99+495=594。拿到阳性的人里，真正患病的比例是 99/594 ≈ 16.7%。

写成公式：P(患病|阳性) = P(患病)×P(阳性|患病) ÷ P(阳性)。分子是'真患者中被检出阳性的部分'，分母是'所有阳性者'，这就是贝叶斯公式。

关键在患病率这个起点：同样99%的准确率，患病率降到千分之一时，阳性后真患病的概率只有约2%。阳性的意义是把怀疑从1%提到17%，要确认还得复检——复检时你的起点已经是17%了。

A cache keeps a copy of expensive data in fast storage: the product page's price is read from the database once, stored in Redis, and the next thousand visitors use the copy instead of hitting the database.

The problem: when the real price changes, the copy still shows the old one. Cache invalidation means deciding when a copy is no longer trustworthy and must be dropped or refreshed.

Two common strategies. TTL: each entry gets a lifetime, say 60 seconds — simple, but for up to a minute users see stale prices. Delete-on-write: when the price updates, delete the cache key, so the next read refetches fresh data.

The hard part is knowing everything that depends on what you changed. The price shows up on the product page, the category listing, the search index, another service's cache — miss one and some users see stale data indefinitely. That's why cache invalidation is famous as a genuinely hard problem.

相关指两个量同涨同跌；因果指改变其中一个，另一个会跟着变。两者可以同时成立，也可以只有相关。

例子：某城市每月冰淇淋销量与溺水人数高度相关。看起来像'吃冰淇淋导致溺水'，但真正驱动两者的是同一件事——夏天气温高：天热买冰淇淋的人多，下水游泳的人也多。这种藏在背后的共同原因叫混杂变量。

判别办法一：分层看数据。只在气温相近的日子内部比较，冰淇淋销量和溺水的相关性会明显减弱甚至消失。办法二：随机实验——随机让一半城区的商店停售冰淇淋，若溺水率没变，因果链就被切断了；若真有因果，差异会显现。

要点：控制共同原因后仍然稳定的关联，或随机实验里出现的差异，才更接近因果。相关是线索，机制和实验才是证据。

Compound growth means each period's gain is a percentage of the current total, so past gains start earning their own gains.

Put 1,000 yuan at 10% per year. Year 1: 1,100. Year 2: interest is 10% of 1,100 — 110, not 100 — giving 1,210. Year 3: 1,331. Simple interest would pay 300 in total; compounding pays 331, and the gap widens every year because the base keeps growing. The formula is principal × (1 + rate)^years.

Why the starting amount matters: everything gets multiplied by the same factor, so proportions are identical but absolute gains scale with the base. After five years, 1,000 becomes 1,611 while 10,000 becomes 16,105 — the extra 9,000 you started with was itself invested and compounded.

Starting time works the same way: each extra year adds one more multiplication. At 7% per year, ten extra years roughly doubles the final amount.

过拟合是模型把训练数据里的噪声也当成了规律：记住了'考题'，没学会'知识'。

类比一个学生：把练习册每道题的答案死记硬背，练习册重做满分；一到考试遇到新题就崩溃。他没有掌握能迁移的规律，只是复述见过的样本。机器学习模型同理：参数太多、训练太久，会把训练数据里的偶然波动（抽样误差、录入错误）也拟合进去。

怎么辨认：模型在训练数据上表现很好，换一批新数据明显变差——这个落差就是标志。所以实践中要留出一部分数据当'考试卷'，训练时不让模型碰，最后用它检验真实水平。

应对办法：增加数据量，让偶然模式藏不住；或者限制模型复杂度，强迫它只学大规律。判断标准始终是新数据上的表现，训练集上的高分不算数。

Suppose you search 'jaguar habitat' and the engine shows 10 results, of which only 3 are about the animal; the other 7 are about the car.

Precision asks: of what was returned, how much was right? 3/10 = 30%. It measures the noise you must wade through — precision 100% means every shown result is relevant, even if many good pages were missed.

Recall asks: of all relevant pages that exist, how many did we find? If 12 good pages exist, recall is 3/12 = 25%. It measures what was missed — recall 100% means nothing relevant was left behind, even if you're flooded with junk.

The two pull against each other: showing 100 results might capture all 12 relevant pages (recall 100%) while precision drops to 12%. Which to prioritize depends on the cost of each error: a cancer screen tolerates false alarms, so it chases recall; a spam filter that hides real emails causes damage, so it chases precision.

自然选择逐代改变的是种群的构成，单个个体的特征终生不变。

长颈鹿并非'伸脖子够树叶所以脖子变长'。真实过程：群体中随机出现各种脖子长度——变异本身不瞄准目标；能吃到高处树叶的个体饿死得少、繁殖得多，长脖子的倾向传给后代；一代代筛选下来，'长脖'基因的频率越来越高。先有随机差异，后有环境筛选，个体从未主动改变自己的基因。

成立需要三个条件：特征可遗传、个体间繁殖成功率有差异、资源有限造成竞争。缺一个，频率就不会定向改变。

常见误读是'用进废退'：那是拉马克的说法——后天越用越发达的器官并不写进基因。进化没有目的，也没有'更高等'的方向，只有当下环境下哪种繁殖策略留下的后代更多。

An operation is idempotent if doing it once or many times leaves the same final result. 'Set email to x@y.com' is idempotent; 'append this coupon to the account' is not.

Why distributed systems care: a network timeout doesn't tell you whether the server processed your request — it may have died after committing but before replying. The only safe response is to retry, so your server will see the same request twice.

If 'charge $100' runs twice, the customer pays twice. The standard fix is an idempotency key: the client generates a unique ID for each logical operation and sends it with every retry; the server records processed keys and, on duplicates, returns the original result instead of acting again.

Design rule: any request that can be retried should be safe to retry.

信息熵衡量'平均需要多少信息才能确定结果'，公式 H = -Σ p·log₂p。概率越小的结果，log₂(1/p) 越大：罕见事件一旦发生，意外感最强。

对比两个硬币：正反各半的均匀硬币，熵为1比特；正面概率0.99的硬币，熵约0.08比特。差别在哪？扔作弊硬币你几乎总能猜中'正面'，别人几乎不必告诉你结果；扔均匀硬币猜哪面都只有一半把握，必须听答案。

这就是均匀分布更不确定的原因：概率一有偏向，'押常见结果'就经常成功，偏向本身是可利用的信息；完全均匀时没有任何偏向可用。数学上可以证明，结果个数固定时各概率相等恰好使熵最大。

注意前提：'均匀最不确定'只在取值个数相同时成立。三项均匀分布的熵约1.58比特，比两项均匀的1比特更不确定——选项越多本来就更难猜。

Deadlock is a cycle of waiting where every participant holds something the next one needs, so none can ever move.

Example: functions Transfer and Audit each need two locks, on Accounts and on Ledger. Transfer takes the Accounts lock, then asks for Ledger; Audit takes Ledger, then asks for Accounts. With unlucky timing, Transfer grabs Accounts while Audit grabs Ledger, and each blocks waiting for the other. Neither will release what it holds until it finishes, and neither can finish — both wait forever.

The cycle needs four conditions at once: exclusive locks, holding one while waiting for another, no way to forcibly take a lock away, and the waits forming a circle. Break any one condition and deadlock disappears.

Simplest fix: a global lock order — every function takes the Accounts lock before the Ledger lock. With no circular wait possible, one function always gets through and the other just waits its turn.

公共物品是这类东西：没法阻止没付钱的人使用，而且一个人用不减少别人能用到的量。路灯、防洪堤、国防、干净的空气都是。对比一个面包：你不付钱拿不到，我吃了你就吃不到。

问题出在'没法排除'。假设小区想装路灯，成本10万，全小区的照明收益加起来有15万，整体划算。但每家都会想：反正别人装了我也能照亮，不如自己不掏钱。结果人人都等别人出钱，路灯装不起来——收益15万的事没发生。这就是搭便车：不付出成本，坐享他人提供的好处。

所以公共物品常由税收供养的政府提供，绕开自愿付费；或者靠选择性激励，比如开源软件给贡献者声誉和职业机会，捐赠榜公示名单。判断一件事会不会'人人指望别人、最后没人做'，先看它是不是公共物品。

Little's law: in a stable queueing system, L = λW — the average number of items in the system equals the arrival rate times the average time each item spends in the system.

Coffee shop example: 10 customers arrive per minute, and a typical customer spends 3 minutes from joining the line to getting coffee. On average, 30 people are inside (10/min × 3 min). Intuition: during the 3 minutes you're there, new customers keep arriving at 10 per minute, so about 30 are present at any moment.

It's an identity about long-run averages, holding for any stable system regardless of how arrivals fluctuate or how you pick who's next — no Poisson or FIFO assumptions needed.

Practical use: measure any two, compute the third. A team has 20 tasks in progress and finishes 5 per day, so an average task takes 4 days. To shorten waiting time W while arrival stays fixed, you must reduce the inventory L.
